key_decisions.decision: Input synchronization for asynchronous GPIO sources
key_decisions.ma_choice: A per-source SYNC_MASK parameter, defaulting to all 1s, puts a 2-FF synchronizer on selected bits. Synchronous sources can bypass it and save 2 cycles.
key_decisions.plan_choice: A fixed 2-FF synchronizer on all 32 sources. A per-source mask is mentioned only as a possible change if D2 is revisited.
key_decisions.note: The default behaviour is identical. The plan just lacks the bypass parameter, which affects only latency for synchronous sources.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Rising-edge detect into a latched epend_q for edge sources, and the live synchronized level for level sources. A new edge wins over a claim or software clear in the same cycle.
key_decisions.plan_choice: Sync flops, a delayed copy for edge detect and a pending flop, muxed by trigger type. Level pending is the unlatched synchronized line, and set wins.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Pending is captured independently of enable. Enable gates only eligibility.
key_decisions.plan_choice: D3: pending captures edges regardless of enable.

key_decisions.ma_choice: 4-bit nibbles (3 bits used), 8 sources per word, 4 words.

key_decisions.decision: Software clear of stuck edge pending
key_decisions.ma_choice: PENDING is read-only. A separate write-1-to-clear PEND_CLR register clears edge latches.
[31] VALID, [4:0] ID with IDs 0..31. An empty claim returns 0 with no side effect.
A 5-level combinational 32-to-1 max-finder (lowest ID wins ties) registered once into best_{vld,id,prio}_q. Threshold and nesting are applied after the register.
key_decisions.plan_choice: D7: a 5-level compare tree with a registered winner {valid, id, prio}. Threshold and running level are folded into eligibility before the tree.
key_decisions.note: Where the threshold is applied differs slightly. The winner selection is equivalent.

key_decisions.ma_choice: eff_thr = max(THRESHOLD, highest in-service level); a source is claimable only if prio > eff_thr.
key_decisions.plan_choice: D8: eligible iff prio > THRESHOLD and prio > running priority.

key_decisions.ma_choice: irq = best_vld_q && best_prio_q > eff_thr. This is combinational from registered state, so irq drops the cycle after a claim edge because isr_v updates immediately.
key_decisions.plan_choice: irq is driven directly from the registered winner-valid flop, with eligibility computed before the register. irq can stay high 1-2 cycles after a claim, and firmware must tolerate a spurious CLAIM.
key_decisions.note: The plan's output is glitch-free but adds a cycle of stale irq after claim/complete. Both are defensible. The plan explicitly documents the spurious-claim consequence.

key_decisions.decision: Claim correctness against a stale tree result
key_decisions.ma_choice: The claim re-checks live state in the same cycle: elig[best_id_q] and the live prio_q[best_id_q] > eff_thr. The in-service level is taken from the live prio_q, guaranteeing a free, strictly higher level and a valid LIFO.
key_decisions.plan_choice: No live re-check. The plan only invalidates the winner register in the cycle after a claim to stop double claims. The claim commits using the registered winner's prio.
key_decisions.note: Without a re-check, the plan can hand out a source that was disabled, dropped its level or was reprogrammed during the stale cycle. It can also record a level from stale prio, breaking the guarantee that the claimed level is free and above the running level. S9 lists the 'level dropped before claim' case but gives no mechanism.

key_decisions.ma_choice: 7 × {valid, stored 5-bit ID}, one slot per level. COMPLETE clears the highest level whose stored ID matches. A non-matching COMPLETE is ignored, and out-of-order completes are allowed.
key_decisions.plan_choice: D9/D10 from Q1: isr_v[7:1] plus isr_id per level, with the highest-match clear and unmatched writes ignored.

key_decisions.ma_choice: An INSERVICE register with [7:1] level bits and [10:8] effective threshold.
key_decisions.plan_choice: A 7-bit IN_SERVICE register plus optional running priority and per-level IDs.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Edge+sync takes 4 cycles and level+sync takes 3. Without sync it is 2 and 1.
key_decisions.plan_choice: About 4 cycles for an edge (2 sync, 1 pending, 1 winner). Level is implicitly 3.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Active-low rst_n with async assert and sync deassert. All config, pending and in-service state reset to 0, so irq is low.
Switching from edge to level clears the epend_q bit, and the live level is used.
key_decisions.plan_choice: S3 specifies trigger-change behaviour, including clearing stale edge pending.

summary: The plan closely tracks the reference on nearly every architectural choice: gateway structure, enable-independent pending capture, nibble packing, PEND_CLR, CLAIM {VALID,ID}, the 5-level registered tree, max(threshold, running level) eligibility, the per-level {v,id} in-service stack with highest-match COMPLETE, reset and latency. There are two equivalent differences. The plan synchronizes all sources without a SYNC_MASK bypass, and it registers irq straight from winner-valid, which adds a cycle of stale irq after claim. The one material gap is that the plan lacks a same-cycle live re-check of eligibility at claim time. It relies only on invalidating the winner after a claim and commits the claim level from the stale registered prio. That can hand out ineligible sources and break the free/strictly-higher-level invariant that the MA guarantees. Both questions were legitimate, since the spec is silent on out-of-order COMPLETE matching and on the empty-CLAIM encoding.
